senses.def: to make something smaller or less in size, amount, or price
examples: Regular exercise can reduce the risk of heart disease.
The store reduced prices on all winter coats.

senses.def: to bring someone or something into a worse state (reduce to)
examples: The fire reduced the old theater to ashes.
The sad ending reduced her to tears.

senses.def: the act of making something smaller or less, or the amount by which it is made less
examples: The new law led to a 20 percent reduction in traffic deaths.
Customers will see a reduction in their monthly bills.

note: Use "a reduction in" something, not "of" ("a reduction in costs").

senses.def: to mention or speak about someone or something (refer to)
examples: In his speech, he referred to the recent floods.
She never refers to her ex-husband by name.

senses.def: to send someone to another person or place for help, advice, or a decision
examples: My doctor referred me to a specialist for further tests.

senses.def: to look at something for information, or (of a word) to describe or mean something
examples: Please refer to the manual for setup instructions.
The term "millennials" refers to people born between about 1981 and 1996.

note: Always "refer to". Spelling: referred, referring (double r).

senses.def: an official who controls a game in sports like soccer, basketball, or boxing
examples: The referee gave him a red card for the tackle.
Fans booed the referee after the controversial call.

senses.def: (British) a person who gives information about your character and abilities for a job application
examples: Please list two referees who can comment on your work.

note: In baseball and tennis, Americans say "umpire". For job applications, Americans say "reference" rather than "referee".

senses.def: something you say or write that mentions someone or something
examples: The movie is full of references to classic horror films.
She made no reference to the scandal in her speech.

senses.def: the act of looking at something for information, or a source of information
examples: Keep the user guide for future reference.
The paper includes a full list of references at the end.

senses.def: a letter or person describing your character and abilities, for a new job
examples: My former boss agreed to give me a reference.

senses.def: a vote in which all the people of a country or area decide on one important issue
examples: The country held a referendum on whether to change the constitution.
Voters rejected the proposal in a referendum last spring.

note: Plural: referendums or (formal) referenda. In US states, such votes are often called "ballot measures".

senses.def: to improve something by making small changes to it
examples: The team spent months refining the design of the app.
Researchers are refining their methods based on early results.

senses.def: to make a natural substance pure by removing other substances from it
examples: Crude oil is refined to make gasoline and diesel.

note: "Refined" can also describe a person who is elegant and well-mannered.

senses.def: to send back light, heat, or sound, or to show an image on a surface
examples: The mountains were reflected in the still lake.
White surfaces reflect sunlight and stay cooler.

senses.def: to show or be a sign of something, such as an attitude or situation
examples: The rise in prices reflects higher energy costs.
Her choices reflect her values.

senses.def: to think carefully and seriously about something
examples: He took some time off to reflect on his career.

note: "Reflect badly/well on someone" = give a bad/good impression of them.

senses.def: an image seen in a mirror, on water, or on another shiny surface
examples: She looked at her reflection in the shop window.
The reflection of the trees on the lake was beautiful.

senses.def: careful thought about something, or an opinion formed after such thought
examples: On reflection, I think we made the right decision.
The book is full of reflections on aging.

senses.def: a sign or result of something
examples: The empty stores are a reflection of the weak economy.

senses.def: a change made to a system, law, or organization to improve it
examples: The government promised major reforms to the health care system.
Many voters support immigration reform.

senses.def: to improve a system or organization by changing it
examples: The new mayor has pledged to reform the police department.

senses.def: to improve your behavior, or to make someone behave better
examples: He was a heavy gambler, but he reformed after his son was born.

senses.def: shelter or protection from danger or trouble, or a place that provides it
examples: Hikers took refuge in a cave during the storm.
Thousands sought refuge across the border.

senses.def: a protected area where wild animals can live safely
examples: The wildlife refuge is home to more than 200 species of birds.

senses.def: a person who has been forced to leave their country because of war or danger
examples: Millions of refugees fled the war and crossed into neighboring countries.
The city opened a new center to help refugees find jobs.

note: An "asylum seeker" has applied for protection but has not yet been officially accepted as a refugee.

senses.def: the act of saying or showing that you will not do, give, or accept something
examples: His refusal to apologize made the situation worse.
The bank's refusal of the loan forced them to sell the house.

senses.def: to say or show that you will not do, accept, or give something
examples: The witness refused to answer any more questions.
She was refused entry to the club because she didn't have ID.

note: Pattern: refuse TO do. The noun "refuse" /ˈrefjuːs/ (formal) means garbage.

senses.def: to get back something you have lost, such as an ability, quality, or control
examples: It took her months to regain her strength after the illness.
The rebels regained control of the city.

senses.def: to think about someone or something in a particular way
examples: She is widely regarded as the best surgeon in the state.
Many people regard the plan with suspicion.

senses.def: respect or admiration for someone, or attention and care
examples: I have a high regard for her work.
He drove fast, without any regard for safety.

senses.def: friendly greetings (regards), often at the end of a message
examples: Give my regards to your parents.
Kind regards, and see you next week.

note: "With regard to" (singular) or "as regards" = about. Not "with regards to" in formal writing.

senses.tr: her şeye rağmen, yine de, ne olursa olsun
senses.def: without paying attention to problems or difficulties; anyway
examples: The weather was terrible, but we went hiking regardless.
He knew the risks but carried on regardless.

senses.def: without being affected by something (regardless of)
examples: Everyone is welcome, regardless of age or background.

note: "Irregardless" is nonstandard; use "regardless".

senses.def: a government, especially one that was not elected fairly and controls people strictly
examples: The military regime banned all opposition parties.
Thousands fled the country to escape the regime.

senses.def: a system or set of rules for managing something
examples: The new tax regime favors small businesses.

note: Usually negative when used for governments. Do not confuse with "regimen" (a diet or exercise plan).

senses.def: a large area of a country or the world, often without exact borders
examples: The region is famous for its wine.
Heavy snow is expected in mountain regions tonight.

senses.def: a part of the body
examples: He felt a sharp pain in the lower back region.

note: "In the region of" means approximately: "in the region of $5 million".

senses.def: relating to a particular region
examples: The restaurant serves regional dishes from southern Italy.
Regional airports have lost many flights to big hubs.

senses.def: to put your name or something's details on an official list
examples: You must register to vote at least 30 days before the election.
The car is registered in my wife's name.

senses.def: an official list or record of names or items
examples: The hotel asked us to sign the guest register.

senses.def: (American) a machine in a store that keeps money and records sales (cash register)
examples: Please pay at the register by the door.

senses.def: to show a measurement or feeling, or to notice something
examples: The earthquake registered 6.2 on the Richter scale.
It took a moment for the news to register.

senses.def: the act of putting a name or details on an official list
examples: Online registration for the conference closes on Friday.
Voter registration has increased sharply among young people.

senses.def: an official document for a vehicle, or (British) a car's license plate number
examples: The officer asked to see my license and registration.

note: In the US, a car's number is the "license plate"; "registration" is the document.

senses.def: to feel sorry or sad about something you did or did not do
examples: I regret not studying harder in college.
You'll regret it if you don't take this chance.

senses.def: (formal) used to say politely that you are sorry about something
examples: We regret to inform you that your flight has been canceled.

senses.def: a feeling of sadness about something you did or did not do
examples: She has no regrets about leaving her job.
He expressed deep regret for the accident.

note: "Regret doing" = sorry about a past action; "regret to do" = sorry about what you are going to say (formal).

senses.def: happening at the same times or with the same space between each one
examples: Regular exercise is good for your mental health.
The buses run at regular intervals throughout the day.

senses.def: doing something often, or usual and normal
examples: She's a regular customer at the café.
I'll just have my regular order, please.

senses.def: (American) of standard or medium size, or ordinary
examples: Can I get a regular coffee and a large orange juice?

senses.def: often, or at regular times
examples: She regularly volunteers at the animal shelter.
Change your passwords regularly to stay safe online.

senses.def: to control an activity or industry using rules
examples: The government regulates the sale of alcohol and tobacco.
Some lawmakers want to regulate social media companies more strictly.

senses.def: to control the speed, temperature, or amount of something so it works properly
examples: Sweating helps the body regulate its temperature.

senses.def: an official rule made by a government or other authority
examples: New safety regulations require all workers to wear helmets.
The restaurant was closed for breaking health regulations.

senses.def: control of something by means of rules
examples: Banks have called for less regulation of the financial sector.

senses.def: a person or organization that officially controls an industry to make sure it operates fairly
examples: Banking regulators fined the company $50 million.
The energy regulator approved the price increase.

senses.def: a device that controls pressure, temperature, or flow in a machine
examples: Divers check the regulator on their air tank before each dive.

note: In news headlines, regulators are often called "watchdogs".

senses.def: having the power to control an industry or activity through rules
examples: The drug still needs regulatory approval before it can be sold.
Regulatory agencies are investigating the bank.

senses.def: the process of helping someone return to a normal life after illness, injury, addiction, or prison
examples: After the knee surgery, he spent six weeks in rehabilitation.
The program focuses on the rehabilitation of young offenders.

senses.def: the process of returning a building or area to good condition
examples: The rehabilitation of the old train station cost $40 million.

note: Informally shortened to "rehab", especially for addiction treatment: "go to rehab".

senses.def: the period during which a king, queen, or emperor rules
examples: The castle was built during the reign of Henry VIII.
Her reign lasted more than sixty years.

senses.def: to rule as a king, queen, or emperor
examples: The emperor reigned for over forty years.

senses.def: (of a feeling or situation) to be the main feature of a place or time
examples: Chaos reigned at the airport after the power outage.
She is the reigning world champion.

note: Same pronunciation as "rain" and "rein". "Give free rein" (not "reign") = allow full freedom.

senses.def: to make an idea, feeling, or belief stronger
examples: The study reinforces the link between sleep and memory.
Ads like this reinforce gender stereotypes.

senses.def: to make a structure or group stronger, e.g. by adding material or more people
examples: Engineers reinforced the old bridge with steel beams.
More troops were sent to reinforce the border.

senses.def: to refuse to accept, believe, or consider something
examples: The board rejected the proposal by a vote of 7 to 2.
Voters rejected the tax increase.

senses.def: to refuse to accept someone for a job or course, or to refuse to love or support someone
examples: Her application was rejected by three universities.
He felt rejected by his own family.

note: Stress: verb re-JECT, noun REE-ject (a thing or person that has been rejected).

senses.def: the act of refusing to accept or consider something
examples: The rejection of the peace plan led to more fighting.
She got a rejection letter from the publisher.

senses.def: the feeling of not being loved or wanted
examples: Fear of rejection stopped him from asking her out.

senses.def: to show or be a connection between two or more things
examples: The study relates diet to heart health.
Most of the questions relate to the company's finances.

senses.def: to understand someone's situation or feelings because you have had similar experiences
examples: I can really relate to the main character in that show.

senses.def: (formal) to tell a story or describe events
examples: She related the details of her journey across the desert.

note: "Relatable" (informal) = easy to identify with: "a relatable character".

senses.def: connected with something in some way
examples: Police are investigating two related crimes in the area.
Stress-related illnesses are becoming more common.

senses.def: in the same family
examples: Are you related to the woman who owns the bakery?

senses.def: the way people, groups, or countries behave toward each other (usually relations)
examples: Relations between the two countries have improved.
The company works hard to maintain good relations with its customers.

senses.def: the way two things are connected
examples: The fee bears no relation to the actual cost of the service.
I have a question in relation to my bill.

senses.def: a member of your family
examples: We're spending the holidays with relations in Texas.

note: For family members, "relative" is more common than "relation" in American English.

senses.def: the way two people or groups feel about and behave toward each other
examples: She has a close relationship with her grandmother.
The relationship between the coach and the players broke down.

senses.def: a romantic or sexual connection between two people
examples: They've been in a relationship for three years.

senses.def: the way two or more things are connected
examples: Researchers studied the relationship between screen time and sleep.

senses.def: a member of your family
examples: We have relatives in Ohio and Michigan.
Only close relatives were invited to the funeral.

senses.def: considered or judged by comparison with something else
examples: After years of war, the country is enjoying relative peace.
Beauty is relative; everyone has different tastes.

note: "Relative to" means compared with: "Prices are low relative to income."

senses.def: to a fairly large degree, especially compared with other things
examples: The test was relatively easy compared with last year's.
The disease is relatively rare in young children.

senses.def: to rest and become calm, or to make a part of your body less tight
examples: I like to relax with a good book on Sunday afternoons.
Take a deep breath and relax your shoulders.

senses.def: to make rules or controls less strict
examples: The city relaxed parking rules during the holidays.

senses.def: calm and not worried or nervous
examples: You seem very relaxed after your vacation.
The restaurant has a relaxed, friendly atmosphere.

senses.def: not strict
examples: The company has a relaxed dress code on Fridays.

note: Relaxed = how a person feels; relaxing = something that makes you feel relaxed.

senses.def: helping you to rest and feel calm
examples: We had a relaxing weekend at the beach.
A hot bath is very relaxing after a long day.

senses.def: to let someone or something go free
examples: The prisoner was released after serving ten years.
The hostages were released unharmed.

senses.def: to make a film, album, product, or information available to the public
examples: The band will release their new album in March.
Police have not released the victim's name.

senses.tr: tahliye, serbest bırakılma; yayın, piyasaya çıkış
senses.def: the act of setting someone free, or of making something available to the public
examples: Her family campaigned for her release.
The film's release has been delayed until next year.

senses.def: to let a substance flow out
examples: The factory released toxic chemicals into the river.

note: A "press release" is an official statement given to journalists.

senses.def: how closely something is connected to the subject or situation
examples: I don't see the relevance of your question to this discussion.
The book still has great relevance today.

senses.def: closely connected with the subject or situation you are dealing with
examples: Please include all relevant documents with your application.
Is that really relevant to what we're discussing?

senses.def: having ideas or value that are useful to people today
examples: The museum is trying to stay relevant to younger visitors.

note: Opposite: irrelevant. Use "relevant to", not "relevant with".

senses.def: the quality of being able to be trusted or of working well consistently
examples: The car is known for its reliability and low running costs.
Experts questioned the reliability of the witness's testimony.

senses.def: able to be trusted to do something well, or likely to be correct
examples: I need a reliable car for my long commute.
We got the information from a reliable source.

senses.def: the happy feeling when something unpleasant stops or does not happen
examples: It was a huge relief to hear that everyone was safe.
She breathed a sigh of relief when the plane landed.

senses.def: the reduction of pain or discomfort
examples: This cream gives quick relief from itching.

senses.def: food, money, or supplies given to people in need, especially after a disaster
examples: Aid groups are sending relief to the earthquake zone.

senses.def: to reduce or remove pain or an unpleasant feeling or problem
examples: The medicine should relieve your headache within an hour.
Building a new road will relieve traffic in the town center.

senses.def: to replace someone at work, or to take a job or duty away from someone
examples: The night nurse relieves her at 11 p.m.
The manager was relieved of his duties after the scandal.

note: "Relieve yourself" is a polite way to say go to the toilet.
